chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Whenever you want to drink water at night, stir the water and say:
'O water, the water of Zamzam and the water of the Euphrates convey to you their greetings.'

key_terms.زَمْزَمَ: Zamzam — the sacred well in Mecca, blessed water associated with the story of Hajar and Ismail
key_terms.فُرَاتٍ: Euphrates (Furat) — major river in Iraq, held in special reverence in Shia tradition due to its association with Karbala
key_terms.يُقْرِئَانِكَ السَّلَامَ: they convey to you greetings — a dual verb form, personifying the two waters as sending salutations

ai.seo_question: What du'a did Imam al-Sadiq prescribe for drinking water at night?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a ritual act and verbal formula to be performed when drinking water at night. The believer is instructed to stir the water and address it directly, invoking the sacred waters of Zamzam (the blessed well in Mecca) and the Euphrates (a river revered in Shia tradition, associated with Karbala). The formula personifies these sacred waters as sending greetings, embedding a moment of spiritual connection within the mundane act of drinking at night.
